text: A failed attempt can remain represented as an option with a failed result.
Failure of one attempt does not state the status of every other attempt.
Retaining an alternative can have a resource cost.
The source hope and sure labels can refer to distinct objects.
An attempted change has a result that can be described.
The selected next attempt can differ from the retained failed attempt.
A failure can constrain a narrower proposition than the original broad goal.
Interest in investigating is not the same variable as the truth of a claim.
The future alternative space contains meaningful distinctions.
Changing conditions can change whether a replay tests the same proposition.
A useful retained record must remain retrievable for a live query.
Benefit from this map must be evaluated on a later operation.
The option can be retained with its result, removed, or retained without its result.
This is an instance of retaining a tested alternative; siblings include a rejected hypothesis and a completed experiment.
A retained option has an identity that distinguishes it from its verdict.
A present failure and a later changed-condition attempt occupy different times.
Other attempts can be untested, independently failed, or successful within another scope.
Number of tested attempts ranges from one to all members of a declared finite set.
Attempt identity and evaluation scope are separate axes.
A current model can track the set; a human may or may not experience encouragement from it.
Retention cost may be one row, a large source bundle, or a repeated expensive operation.
Retain a pointer, retain full evidence, or regenerate from a verified source.
A single rejected option and hundreds of rejected options create different retrieval spaces.
An available pointer still resolves when used; if not, its preservation is only nominal.
Left and right propositions can be identical or different.
The certainty predicate may apply to one tested outcome while the future option set has many members.
A relation between two attitudes is a binary relation; siblings include compatibility, support and tension.
The relation’s actual operands are supplied rather than inferred from labels.
Result can be observed, ambiguous, absent or conditional.
Model output, source assertion and human experience are different result channels.
A reviewer can inspect an output without observing the user’s experience.
Immediate output and delayed transfer are different observations.
Repeat unchanged, change conditions, choose a sibling, or defer selection.
A next-attempt choice is a portfolio allocation; siblings include replication and boundary testing.
Similarity to the earlier attempt can range from an exact replay to a new target.
A one-slot choice and a four-slot portfolio admit different diversity constraints.
Scope can be an input, a procedure implementation, a target class or a universal claim.
A failed implementation can coexist with an unresolved underlying idea.
The failure observation actually bears on the proposition being narrowed.
A source defender may attribute failure to implementation; a critic may target the proposition. Both require a discriminator.
Investigation priority is a selection judgment; truth is an epistemic property.
An interesting claim can be false, unresolved or established.
Novelty, tractability and consequence can vary independently of truth status.
A resolved false claim can still motivate a later mechanism question.
Maybe as p>0 includes p=1; maybe as 0<p<1 does not.
Logical possibility and strict uncertainty are two candidate senses.
The sure/positive overlap and sure/strict exclusion occupy different cells in SE35.
The chosen meaning is declared for the fixture; the source intended meaning may remain unknown.
A changed source version creates a new input at a later time.
Change can concern price, actor, tool, semantics or opportunity window.
A replay can replicate, extend or fail to address the earlier claim.
The recorded changed condition is causally or logically relevant, rather than decorative.
The next model reader needs the discriminating condition; the author may need literal fidelity.
Search key can be verdict, obstacle, target or source.
Chronology and a scoped index support different corpus sizes.
A concise index can coexist with complete underlying records.
The map can change an input, remain unused, or repeat what was already known.
A changed operation has an inspectable before/input and after/output.
The user’s appraisal is a separate observation from the model’s output difference.
Present use does not establish future transfer.
